title: Actual quotient-cone scalar comparisons for a fixed reconstruction family
statement: Fix the datum, prime, algebraic closure and finite coefficient fields of [def-pod-reconstruction-common-stage-data], with ell different from the residue characteristic. Supply a normalized CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus A_E for each field and any family R_E of the actual integral and raw rational reconstruction functors with their actual units. For every E ≤ L there are integral comparison isomorphisms b_{L/E} and raw rational comparison isomorphisms beta_{L/E}. The integral comparison satisfies SameIndexRealization, including all quotient augmentations, scalar counit coordinates and completed conjugation; its composite with the inverse target unit equals scalar extension of the inverse source unit. The rational component is Q_L(b_C) and satisfies the corresponding inverse-unit equation on every rational object. No identity or associator equation, representative transport, functor descent or common-stage isomorphism is asserted.

source.place: First sentence, identity compact support; Step 1 of lem-pod-reconstruction-common-stage-coherence.

proof.text: For each inclusion construct the actual quotient-cone comparison with completionUnitScalarIntertwining. Compare its chosen coefficient calculi with the supplied A_E and A_L using the normalized quotient/reduction models and their adjunction-unit equations. The quotient-tower identification preserves augmentations and the counit realization on resolving complexes, and hence transports the entire same-index formula and completed conjugation. Restrict to complete constructible objects and transport along integral_actual. The specified scalar comparison and units are invertible on these inputs, giving b and its inverse-unit equation.

proof.text: Apply the semilinear raw rationalization construction of reconstructionRawRationalNaturality to this fixed integral comparison, rather than choosing a new reconstruction family. Balancing, naturality and invertibility descend on tensor Hom groups. Its components are Q_L(b_C). Localizing the inverse-unit equation and using the actual localized unit components gives the rational inverse-unit equation. Finally identify the redundant scalar parameters and transport along the published equalities defining the stage transitions. The inverse-unit equation uniquely determines both comparisons, including at identity inclusions and ramified extensions.

theorem reconstructionScalarRealizations (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (R : ∀ E, Realization D l Ω E (A E)) :
    ∃ (b : ∀ (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L),
        (R E).integral ⋙ integralTransition l Ω (point D) E L h ≅
          integralTransition l Ω (point D) E L h ⋙ (R L).integral)
      (β : ∀ (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L),
        (R E).rational ⋙ stageTransition l Ω (point D) E L h ≅
          stageTransition l Ω (point D) E L h ⋙ (R L).rational),
      (∀ (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L), SameIndexRealization D l Ω A R E L h (b E L h)) ∧
      (∀ (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L)
        (C : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω E) (point D)),
        (b E L h).hom.app C ≫ (R L).integralUnit.inv.app
            ((integralTransition l Ω (point D) E L h).obj C) =
          (integralTransition l Ω (point D) E L h).map ((R E).integralUnit.inv.app C)) ∧
      (∀ (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L) (C : Stage l Ω (point D) E),
        HEq ((β E L h).hom.app C)
          ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L) (point D)).map
            ((b E L h).hom.app C.obj))) ∧
      (∀ (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L) (C : Stage l Ω (point D) E),
        (β E L h).hom.app C ≫ (R L).rationalUnit.inv.app
            ((stageTransition l Ω (point D) E L h).obj C) =
          (stageTransition l Ω (point D) E L h).map ((R E).rationalUnit.inv.app C))
